battle.name: 加達拉之戰
battle.brief: 公元前93年，納巴泰王奧布達斯在約旦河東岸加達拉與雅穆克河谷一帶設伏，擊潰哈斯蒙尼王亞歷山大·雅奈烏斯的遠征軍；雅奈烏斯僅以身免，退回耶路撒冷，東岸諸城盡失。卡面的希臘重步兵是這支軍隊的戰術血統：方陣盾牆在狹窄山谷中反成累贅，被駱駝與輕騎衝散。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前93年爆發於約旦河東岸的哈斯蒙尼與納巴泰之戰，交戰雙方都是前一個世紀新近崛起、同樣靠商路立國的王國。哈斯蒙尼一方是猶太王國，以耶路撒冷為都，國王亞歷山大·雅奈烏斯在父親約翰·海爾卡努斯二世於前103年去世之後取得王位；國家的軍隊骨幹是按希臘式操練的重裝步兵與其方陣，輔以弓箭手、投射兵與少量騎兵，並徵用猶大、以邊、佩阿等地的輔助部隊，國王本人常在野戰軍之前行軍，戰利品與輜重由後隊護送。納巴泰一方是佩特拉為中心的阿拉伯王國，國王奧布達斯以商隊稅、牲畜與控制綠洲的權力立國，其軍隊以騎兵、弓手與大量駱駝組成，能在沙漠與丘陵之間長距離機動作戰。戰場周邊還站著三個旁觀者：大馬士革的塞琉古王朝已陷於崩解，北方亞美尼亞與安息尚隔著沙漠與山地，羅馬此時忙於西班牙與地中海的戰事，尚未把手伸進黎凡特。因此這是一場沒有羅馬仲裁、也沒有帝國邊境保護的邊境戰，勝負全由地形與牲畜決定。
countriesEn: This war was fought in 93 BC on the eastern bank of the Jordan, between two kingdoms that had both risen within the previous century and both lived off the caravan roads of the Near East. On one side was the Hasmonean kingdom of Judaea, centred on Jerusalem, ruled by King Alexander Jannaeus, who had taken the throne in 103 BC after the death of his father John Hyrcanus II. The backbone of the Hasmonean army was heavy infantry drilled in Greek fashion and formed into a phalanx, supported by archers, javelinmen, a small body of cavalry, and contingents of auxiliaries drawn from Judaea, Idumea and Perea; the king himself usually marched at the head of the field army, with the booty and baggage guarded by the rear. On the other side was the Arab kingdom of the Nabataeans, centred on Petra, whose king Obodas built his state on caravan tolls, herds and control of the watering places; the Nabataean army consisted of cavalry, archers and a great many camels, and could move for days across desert and broken country. Three onlookers stood around the field: the Seleucid dynasty at Damascus was already coming apart, Armenia and Parthia lay far away beyond desert and mountain, and Rome was absorbed in its Spanish wars and had not yet reached the Levant. There was therefore no Roman arbitration and no imperial border to protect either side: a border war in which terrain and animals decided the issue.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物只有幾位，但每一位都左右了戰局。亞歷山大·雅奈烏斯是這場戰爭的主角：他的父親約翰·海爾卡努斯二世在位時與納巴泰簽有和約，並以王族婚事維繫友好，前103年老王去世、兄弟三人分國之後，雅奈烏斯放棄這份外交，轉而向約旦河東岸與沿海推進，前100年攻下迦薩港，又取阿馬圖斯、摩押、基列與加達拉，把納巴泰商隊的出海口握在自己手中；正是這一步把對手逼到公開對抗。奧布達斯是納巴泰的國王，約瑟夫斯在《猶太戰爭》裡以「阿拉伯人的王奧布達斯」稱之，在《古代史》中又以阿雷塔斯之名記同一人；部分學者認為二者是同一位國王的不同稱呼，也有人認為指的是他的兄弟奧布達斯。無論如何，設伏、驅趕與最後的追擊都由這一方主導。真正把這場戰役留在文獻裡的是約瑟夫斯本人：他先在公元75年前後寫成《猶太戰爭》，又在公元93至94年寫成《古代史》，後者距戰事不足一百八十年，是最接近的記錄；但他站在羅馬讀者的立場，把哈斯蒙尼的敗績寫得沉重。同一段文字還提到「六年之間雙方數戰，所殺猶太人不少於五萬」，這既是記錄，也是修辭。
peopleEn: Only a handful of people are named in the sources, but each of them shaped the outcome. Alexander Jannaeus is the central figure. His father John Hyrcanus II had kept peace with the Nabataeans and sealed it with a dynastic marriage; when the old king died in 103 BC and the kingdom was split among three brothers, Jannaeus let that diplomacy lapse and turned instead toward the east bank of the Jordan and the coast, taking Gaza about 100 BC and then Amathus, Moab, Gilead and Gadara, so that he held the Nabataeans' outlet to the sea. It was that step that forced the confrontation. Obodas was the Nabataean king: Josephus calls him 'Obodas, king of the Arabians' in The Jewish War and writes of the same man as Aretas in the Antiquities; some scholars take the two names for one ruler under different designations, others take the passage to refer to Obodas, brother of the king. Either way the ambush, the driving of the enemy into the ravine and the final pursuit were all directed from the Nabataean side. The man who actually preserved the battle in writing was Josephus himself. He composed The Jewish War around AD 75 and the Antiquities in AD 93-94, the latter less than a century and a half after the fighting, and he wrote for a Roman readership, so he weighed the Hasmonean defeat heavily. The same passage also states that in the interval of six years the two sides fought several battles and that the king slew not fewer than fifty thousand of the Jews, a figure that is at once a record and a rhetorical flourish.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵，裝備的是青銅蒙皮的圓形大盾、亞麻或皮革製成的胸甲、護脛、短矛與佩劍，是公元前五世紀希臘城邦的標準配備，與前93年那場戰鬥相隔四百餘年，本不該出現在那片山谷。但它留下的血統還在：哈斯蒙尼軍隊的重裝步兵正是按馬其頓方陣的樣子操練，短矛換成長逾四公尺的薩里沙長槍，大盾換成小圓盾，彼此遮蔽的動作卻同出一源。約瑟夫斯記下雅奈烏斯在山間與納巴泰人周旋時，靠的正是希臘式的密集隊形與雇傭兵方陣。戰場上真正決定勝負的裝備在另一方：納巴泰的弓手用弓角微曲的複合弓，射程遠於希臘的輕盾投射兵；他們有投槍手、套索手與大量騎兵，坐騎是沙漠與高原培育出的良種；最關鍵的是駱駝，這些傢畜在約瑟夫斯筆下不是運載工具，而是武器：成群的駱駝被用來把擁擠的方陣推壓、踩踏，同時也是全軍數週糧食與水源的載體。鎧甲方面，納巴泰人多用皮甲、鱗甲與小銅盔，沒有希臘重裝步兵那種從肩到膝的整片覆蓋；這意味著他們在正面硬撞時必然輸掉，卻在山峽與亂軍中佔盡便宜。營地與輜重同樣是戰具：遠征軍的帳篷、糧車與器皿一旦被奪，哈斯蒙尼在約旦河東岸的據點就無所依憑。
kitsEn: The card shows a Greek hoplite armed with a bronze-faced round shield, a linen or leather corselet, greaves, a short spear and a sword, the standard kit of a fifth-century BC polis; the gap between that and the battle of 93 BC is about four centuries, and such a man could not have stood in that valley. What survived was the bloodline. The Hasmonean heavy infantry were drilled as a Macedonian phalanx, their short spears exchanged for sarissas more than four metres long and their great shields reduced to small round ones, but the mutual covering of the men was the same habit, and Josephus makes a point of the Greek close order and of the mercenary phalanx with which Jannaeus fought his way through the hill country. The equipment that actually decided the field lay with the other side. Nabataean archers used laminated recurved bows, out-ranging the javelin-armed light infantry of the Greek tradition; they had javelin men, slingers and much cavalry on horses bred for the desert, and the decisive item was the camel. In Josephus's account the camel is not a beast of burden but a weapon: herds of them were used to push, crowd and trample the compressed phalanx, and they carried the food and water on which the whole army depended for weeks. On armour the Nabataeans wore leather, scale and small bronze helmets, without the full shoulder-to-knee covering of a Greek heavy infantryman; that meant they would lose a frontal collision, while gaining everything in a ravine and in a broken melee. Camp and baggage were weapons too: once the tents, wagons and stores of the expedition were taken, the Hasmonean footholds east of the Jordan had nothing to stand on.
tactics: 納巴泰在這場戰鬥裡沒有打一場正面會戰，而是做了一件他們的老本行：讓敵人走進自己選定的地形。前93年，雅奈烏斯率大軍沿約旦河東岸北上，要奪回佩阿與基列的城邑，隊伍拉得很長，家眷、糧車與帳篷跟在中段，側翼只有輕裝的斥候與投射兵護著。奧布達斯把主力藏在雅穆克河谷兩側的丘陵與峽口，等遠征軍進入一段狹窄山溝，再封住出口，兩翼以弓手與投槍手居高覆蓋谷中，同時把駱駝群趕到方陣的正面與側面，靠牲畜的體量與騷動擠亂隊形；山谷沒有縱深，馬其頓式方陣無法展開，盾牌一旦失去互相遮蔽，厚重的正面就變成一批各自為戰的個人。約瑟夫斯寫得直接：全軍在深谷中被「眾多的駱駝」擠碎。哈斯蒙尼一方唯一逃出的，是帶著少數隨從連夜奔回耶路撒冷的國王本人。整場戰鬥的勝負手有三：一是道路知識，納巴泰人熟悉每一條能通車隊的山溝，遠征軍只是在跟著嚮導走；二是水源，沙漠隊伍把敵人拖到飲水與草料難以支撐的地方；三是牲畜，把重步兵的秩序變成一群受驚的人。
tacticsEn: The Nabataeans fought no set-piece battle here; they did what they had always done, and made the enemy walk into ground of their choosing. In 93 BC Jannaeus marched north with a large army along the east bank of the Jordan to recover the towns of Perea and Gilead, the column stretched out with the households, grain wagons and tents in the middle and only light scouts and javelinmen guarding the flanks. Obodas hid his main body in the hills and defiles on both sides of the Yarmouk valley, let the expedition pass into a narrow ravine, closed the exit, put archers and javelinmen on the heights to sweep the valley floor, and at the same time drove his camels against the front and flanks of the phalanx, using the bulk and the noise of the animals to disorder the ranks. A valley has no depth: a Macedonian phalanx cannot deploy, and once the shields cease to cover one another the weight of the front becomes a crowd of men fighting each other. Josephus puts it directly: the whole army was broken to pieces by the multitude of camels in the deep valley. The only Hasmonean to get out was the king himself, who reached Jerusalem with a few followers. Three things decided the day: knowledge of the roads, since the Nabataeans knew every gully that could take wagons and the expedition was merely following guides; water, since a desert column drags its enemy to places where neither drink nor fodder will hold; and animals, which turned the order of heavy infantry into a crowd of frightened men.
data: 可以引用的數字不多，但仍有幾條有據可查。年份是前93年，出處是戰爭列表與相關工具書條目；古代作者沒有記下月份，卡面因此以七月填之，只代表一般推測的作戰季節，並非史實。戰場在加達拉，即今約旦的烏姆凱斯，位置約在北緯32.6度、東經35.7度，屬雅穆克河谷上游的丘陵地帶，約瑟夫斯提到伏擊點在「哥蘭附近」；從耶路撒冷到加達拉約一百三十公里，從佩特拉到加達拉約一百八十公里，這兩個數字說明這是一支可以遠征、但補給線很長的隊伍。兵員兩軍都無從考證，約瑟夫斯只說「眾多的駱駝」與「深谷中的全軍」；他另有一句被後世反覆引用：「六年之間雙方數戰，所殺猶太人不少於五萬」，這是古代記者的修辭數字，不宜當作統計，但可以確定戰爭延續了六年上下，並且以哈斯蒙尼方面的慘重損失收場。城邑的得失是有清單的：戰前雅奈烏斯一方據有加達拉、阿馬圖斯、摩押、基列與迦薩，戰後放棄約旦河東岸四城；羅馬的介入則在更遠的未來，前63年龐培把十日城併入版圖，前106年佩特拉被改組為阿拉伯行省。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are few but real. The year is 93 BC, taken from the standard lists of wars and from the reference entries on the engagement; the ancient authors record no month, so the card fills in July, which marks a presumed campaigning season rather than a fact. The battlefield was Gadara, the modern Umm Qais in Jordan, at roughly 32.6 degrees north and 35.7 degrees east, in the hilly country at the head of the Yarmouk valley; Josephus places the ambush near what he calls Golan. Jerusalem lies about 130 kilometres from Gadara and Petra about 180 kilometres, which says something about an army that could march that far but kept a long supply line. The numbers of men on both sides are simply not recoverable: Josephus speaks only of the multitude of camels and of the whole army in the deep valley. One line of his has been quoted endlessly, that in the interval of six years the two sides fought several battles and he slew not fewer than fifty thousand of the Jews, which is a rhetorical figure of the ancient historian rather than a statistic, though it does establish that the war ran for something like six years and ended in heavy Hasmonean losses. The territorial ledger is clearer: before the battle Jannaeus held Gadara, Amathus, Moab, Gilead and Gaza, and afterwards he gave up the four towns east of the Jordan. Rome's involvement lies further ahead: in 63 BC Pompey took the Decapolis, and in AD 106 Petra was reorganised as the Roman province of Arabia.
cause: 打起來的原因，拆開看有兩層。表面的一層是地盤與商路：前103年老王海爾卡努斯二世去世，兄弟三人分割王國，雅奈烏斯執掌耶路撒冷與猶大，他放棄父輩與納巴泰的和約與姻親關係，把軍隊推向約旦河東岸；前100年他攻下迦薩港，切斷了納巴泰商隊通往地中海的最後出口，又取去摩押、基列與加達拉，等於把對方的核心牧場與關稅站一併拿走。對納巴泰而言，佩特拉的財富來自香料與貨物的過境稅，一旦商隊改道，或者經過迦薩的貨物不再繳納自己的稅關，王室的收入與壟斷地位都會受損，於是佩特拉的出兵不是為了報復，而是為了把商路與牧場拿回來。深一層是區域權力的真空：敘利亞的塞琉古王朝在內戰與外患裡節節敗退，敘利亞與巴勒斯坦一帶出現真空，納巴泰與哈斯蒙尼都趁勢把手伸長；邊境上的小衝突與劫掠多年不絕，終於在一個峽谷裡爆發全戰。羅馬當時忙於西班牙與地中海的戰事，沒有能力仲裁，兩家只能自己解決。
causeEn: There are two layers to the quarrel. On the surface it is a matter of land and trade. When the old king Hyrcanus II died in 103 BC and the kingdom was divided among three brothers, Jannaeus, holding Jerusalem and Judaea, let slip the peace and the marriage alliance his father had kept with the Nabataeans and turned his army east across the Jordan; by about 100 BC he had taken Gaza and cut off the Nabataeans' last outlet to the Mediterranean, and then taken Moab, Gilead and Gadara, which meant carrying away the pastures and the toll-stations on which the other side depended. For the Nabataeans the wealth of Petra came from the transit dues on incense and other goods; if the caravans changed their route, or if the goods passing Gaza no longer paid their customs, both the revenue and the monopoly of the crown would suffer. The expedition from Petra was therefore not revenge but an attempt to take the roads and the pastures back. Underneath that lay a vacuum of regional power: the Seleucid dynasty in Syria was losing ground to civil war and foreign pressure, and both the Nabataeans and the Hasmoneans stretched into the gap. Small clashes and raids along the frontier had gone on for years, and in the end they came to a head in a ravine. Rome at that moment was busy with its wars in Spain and the Mediterranean and had no power to arbitrate, so the two houses had to settle it themselves.
impact: 加達拉的敗仗改寫了黎凡特北部的權力地圖。哈斯蒙尼的東岸擴張就此中止，國王回到耶路撒冷時面對的是因長期戰事而沸騰的國內反對派，約瑟夫斯記下的場面是群眾譴責這位王只會打仗不會治理，隨後發生屠殺與叛亂，王位十年搖搖欲墜；換句話說，一場邊境敗仗變成了哈斯蒙尼王朝內部的清算。納巴泰則相反，國王的威名在民間與商路上傳開，約瑟夫斯寫他此後被自己的國民當作神來敬奉，阿夫達特的納巴泰神廟中至今留有稱他為「神」的碑銘，這是納巴泰王國歷史上第一位受神化的君主。戰略上，納巴泰掌握了十日城與大馬士革至迦薩這條走廊，約旦河東岸的城邑重新回到商旅的保護之下，塞琉古人再想南下也被擋在戈蘭之外；約前87年，塞琉古王安提阿科斯十二世在加達拉一帶與納巴泰交戰，陣亡於陣中，塞琉古勢力就此退出黎凡特南部，納巴泰成為這片地區唯一的主人。長期看，這場戰爭的結果是由羅馬收尾：前63年龐培接管十日城與約旦河以東，前106年佩特拉被改組為羅馬的阿拉伯行省，商隊政治的最後一頁仍然寫著同一條道路。
impactEn: The defeat at Gadara redrew the political map of the northern Levant. Hasmonean expansion east of the Jordan stopped there, and the king came back to Jerusalem to a city boiling with the resentment that years of campaigning had produced; Josephus describes the scene in which the multitude blamed the king for fighting wars and not ruling, and murder and rebellion followed, with the throne shaky for a decade. In short, a border defeat turned into a purge inside the Hasmonean dynasty. For the Nabataeans the effect ran the other way: the king's name travelled among the people and along the caravan roads, and Josephus writes that his subjects came to worship him as a god; in the Nabataean temple at Avdat in the Negev there are inscriptions that call him a god, and he is the first deified king in the history of the Nabataean state. Strategically the Nabataeans now held the Decapolis and the corridor from Damascus to Gaza; the towns east of the Jordan went back under the protection of the caravans, and the Seleucids were kept out beyond Golan. Around 87 BC the Seleucid king Antiochus XII Dionysus fought the Nabataeans in the vicinity of Gadara and was killed in the fighting, the Seleucid presence in the southern Levant was over, and the Nabataeans were left as the only power in the region. In the long run the war was closed by Rome: in 63 BC Pompey took the Decapolis and the lands east of the Jordan, and in AD 106 Petra was reorganised as the Roman province of Arabia, so that the last page of the caravan politics was written along the same road.
result: 就前93年這一天而言，結果是明確的：納巴泰在峽谷裡全勝。雅奈烏斯的遠征軍在深谷中被擠碎，營帳、輜重與攻城器械盡為敵所得，國王本人勉強逃回耶路撒冷；哈斯蒙尼放棄約旦河東岸的加達拉、阿馬圖斯、摩押與基列，以換取納巴泰不去支持耶路撒冷城內的反對派——這是一種以地盤買內安的結局，國王的性命與城門未失，代價是整條東岸。從戰術上看，納巴泰用自己最擅長的辦法贏了這場仗：不與對手在開闊地會戰，不在正面硬撞，而是用道路、伏擊、封口與牲畜，把一支嚴重依賴正面與秩序的方陣軍隊變成被擠壓的散兵。卡面那件希臘重步兵在此的角色也正是在此——它所代表的那種「盾牌相接即為一體」的正面防禦觀念，在山谷裡從優勢變成致命弱點。餘波則長得多：奧布達斯的國威達到頂峰，約旦河東岸重回商旅保護之下，塞琉古人退出南部黎凡特，而這一切最終都會被龐培的羅馬接管，以及前106年阿拉伯行省的設立收尾。
resultEn: For the day in 93 BC the outcome is plain: a complete Nabataean victory. Jannaeus's expedition was crushed in the deep valley, tents, baggage and siege equipment all fell to the enemy, and the king himself barely made it back to Jerusalem; the Hasmoneans gave up Gadara, Amathus, Moab and Gilead east of the Jordan in exchange for the Nabataeans not supporting the opposition inside Jerusalem, land bought with the peace of the capital, the king's life and his walls saved at the price of the whole eastern shore. Tactically, the Nabataeans won in the way they were best at: no pitched battle in the open, no frontal collision, but roads, ambush, a sealed exit and animals, used to turn an army that depended on frontage and order into a crowd pressed together. The hoplite on the card has a precise place in this: the idea it stands for, that a wall of joined shields is one thing rather than many, turns from an advantage into a fatal weakness in a ravine. The consequences run much longer. Obodas's prestige reaches its height, the east bank returns to the protection of the caravans, the Seleucids withdraw from the southern Levant, and all of it is eventually closed by Rome under Pompey and by the establishment of the province of Arabia in AD 106.
